name: Thermobaric Pressure Cestus TPC-2 'Smother'
description:
The TPC-2 is a full-hand combat glove constructed from heat-resistant composite fiber, with a sealed micro-reservoir embedded in the dorsal housing containing a proprietary aerosolized fuel compound designated ARCTURUS FUEL-7. On impact, a pressure-sensitive detonator in the striking surface triggers a controlled thermobaric microexplosion — a burst no larger than a closed fist, but generating an overpressure wave of approximately 14 PSI at point of contact. The explosion is directed forward along the strike axis, meaning the wearer experiences negligible backblast while the target absorbs the full concussive force.

The thermobaric mechanism gives the TPC-2 a deeply unsettling effect profile. The overpressure wave does not cause the clean, visible trauma of a blade wound — it ruptures eardrums, collapses air pockets in lung tissue, and induces severe disorientation through sinus and inner-ear compression. Targets frequently remain standing for several seconds before the neurological cascade catches up with them, creating a delayed-drop phenomenon that experienced users exploit by landing additional strikes before the target falls. In enclosed spaces — corridors, vehicle interiors, elevator shafts — the reflected overpressure compounds the effect dramatically.

ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS positions the TPC-2 as a 'dynamic entry support tool' for military and law enforcement. Its fuel reservoirs are rated for 12 detonations per cartridge, and cartridges are color-coded by yield — gray for standard, amber for elevated, red for breach-grade. Red-cartridge TPC-2 units have been linked to multiple fatalities in poorly ventilated environments, and their sale outside of military channels is explicitly prohibited under GLMZ Municipal Code 7.4.2(c), a law that is enforced approximately never.
specifications:
weight: 1.1 kg per glove
fuel reservoir: 12-strike cartridge, field-replaceable in 8 seconds
overpressure output: 14 PSI at contact point (standard cartridge)
detonation trigger: Pressure-sensitive — activates at 40 N impact force
blast direction: Forward-axis channeled — 92% forward, 8% lateral dispersal
heat resistance: Rated to 1,200°C internal, 200°C external
cartridge variants: Gray (standard), Amber (elevated yield), Red (breach-grade, military restricted)
backblast to user: Negligible on standard and amber; minor thermal sensation on red
tactical_use: Military operators use the TPC-2 in dynamic entry scenarios where firearms are impractical due to ricochet risk or hostage proximity. The standard technique is a palm-strike to the chest — maximizing lung tissue contact — followed by a second strike to the base of the skull once the target drops. In confined corridor fighting, a single amber-cartridge strike can incapacitate multiple targets through reflected overpressure. Operators are trained to avoid using red cartridges in spaces smaller than 20 cubic meters due to documented self-incapacitation risk from reflected wave.
cultural_context: The TPC-2 is one of those weapons that everyone in GLMZ has heard of but almost no one has seen in person, which has made it into something of a myth. Military veterans who served in corporate conflict zones sometimes speak of 'the gloves that knock you down before you know you've been hit.' On the black market, a functioning TPC-2 pair with a full complement of cartridges commands prices that put it out of reach of street-level operators. Those who do carry them are generally operating at a level of violence that transcends street crime — mercenary contracts, corporate war operations, or the kind of personal vendettas that come with institutional backing.
known_users: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS special operations contractors
Former military operators who retained service equipment
One documented use by a GLMZ Transit Authority officer (case under internal review)
story_hooks: A black market arms broker is offering a crate of TPC-2 units with amber cartridges, but the serial numbers have been filed and the fuel compound inside doesn't match ARCTURUS FUEL-7 specifications — someone is manufacturing knockoffs, and the yield variance on the knockoff cartridges is unpredictable.
A veteran with a pair of TPC-2 units is living quietly in the lower districts, but someone has started leaving red cartridges outside their door — a threat, a message, or an invitation.

The players are hired to retrieve a TPC-2 from a crime scene before the municipal investigators catalog it, because the weapon's serial number traces back to an ARCTURUS executive who was supposedly unarmed at the time of death.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist combat glove with pronounced knuckle housings and a sealed dorsal ridge. The striking surface is subtly convex, designed to focus impact force. Entirely enclosed hand covering with minimal finger articulation—built for devastating efficiency rather than dexterity. The overall impression is deliberately heavy and industrial, like a weapon that happens to be worn rather than held.
physical_description.dimensions: Length 28 cm (wrist to fingertip), width 12 cm across knuckles, dorsal height 4.5 cm. Fuel reservoir cartridge slot runs along the back of the hand, approximately 8 cm long and 2 cm wide.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and purposeful—1.1 kg per glove creates noticeable weight distribution when worn, pulling slightly downward at the wrist. Dense enough to feel like a tool of serious intent, but balanced enough that trained operators can sustain strikes for extended periods.
physical_description.primary_material: Heat-resistant composite fiber matrix reinforced with embedded thermal dispersal channels. The striking surface incorporates a harder carbide-polymer blend rated to 1,200°C internal temperature.
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial gray with micro-textured surface to reduce light reflection and improve grip consistency. Areas around the fuel cartridge slot show more pronounced texture from repeated insertions.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal gray primary body with secondary accents: the fuel cartridge slot features a thin red warning line running its length. Small color-coded indicator dots near the wrist denote cartridge type compatibility (gray, amber, red variants). Some units bear subdued reflective trim on the inner wrist for identification in low-light operations.
physical_description.grip_texture: Internal surface features a ribbed thermoplastic elastomer with embedded pressure-distribution channels. The palm area has subtle contouring to distribute impact force evenly across the hand. The wrist closure uses a reinforced hook-and-loop system over a rigid spinal support.
distinctive_features: Pronounced convex striking surface with microscopic pressure-sensing channels
Sealed fuel cartridge slot with color-coded indicator zone
Subtle venting ports along the knuckle ridge—thermobaric signature vents that dissipate internal heat
Reinforced wrist anchor with integrated strain relief
Subtle seam work along the dorsal ridge suggesting internal pressure containment
Impact-absorption gel pockets visible as slightly darker zones beneath the surface
Detonator trigger mechanism recessed into the striking surface (not visually prominent but creates a slight surface irregularity)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Blackwood Commercial Group logo stamped into the inner wrist panel in small raised lettering. Serial number laser-etched along the cartridge slot edge. Small 'ARCTURUS FUEL-7' marking on the cartridge indicator zone. Military-spec units bear a restriction notice: 'MILITARY USE ONLY' engraved in small text on the inner palm.
physical_description.condition_typical: Military issue: well-maintained, no visible damage, but bearing micro-scratches on the striking surface from repeated use and cartridge insertions. Field-deployed units show slight thermal discoloration on the knuckle vents—a pale tan staining from internal heat exposure. Black-market variants (rare) often display improvised cartridge modifications, jury-rigged padding, or replacement fuel system adaptations.
